findings.summary: §1.3 requires the per-drain progress line to carry 第几轮 / drain reason / termination.state / 板面 head_seq, but the emitted line prints attempt, reason, state, coverage, zeroGrowthRounds and drain_id — the board head_seq is absent, and no other per-round output supplies it. E0c1 already exposes a GT-8-safe list-endpoint reader (src/bus.ts readChannelHeadSeqFromList), so the field could be added without touching the single-channel endpoint. Non-blocking: no §2 acceptance criterion (1–11) tests the progress line, exit codes and the per-round record append are unaffected.

findTickTerminationInJournal keeps the LAST *parseable* tick entry rather than the last tick entry, so if a later round's tick emitted an unparseable result (e.g. the '[bash 非零退出 EXIT:n]' shape from GT-5) while an earlier round parsed fine, the stale earlier snapshot is returned instead of the §1.1 loud failure. Impact is bounded: this only matters inside a max_rounds drain (exit 1 skips check-drain-failures.mjs), the returned state stays null, and the entry then fails loudly on the attempt/wall-clock limit rather than reporting success.

Product module branches on process.env.VITEST to decide whether to run its CLI entry point, coupling shipped code to the test framework; the cross-drain test in turn has to scrub VITEST out of the child env for the entry to work. An explicit CLI wrapper (or import.meta.url === argv[1] check) would keep the product path independent of the harness.
Helper _read_drain_termination is defined but never called — the loop inlines the same vite-node invocation at line 426. Dead code that can drift from the real call site.

Header comment still describes archiving 'loop 的 run.stdout.log / run.stderr.log', but the cross-drain loop now writes per-attempt drain-N/drain.stdout.log and drain.stderr.log; no run.stdout.log is produced any more. Content coverage is unchanged (arguably better, since every round is kept), only the comment is stale.

The continuation-gate failure message still reads 'hasPendingWork or termination.state==null && !capHit' while the implemented gate is exactly state === null (hasPendingWork is explicitly voided and capHit deliberately does not stop continuation so in-flight work can drain to 'capped'). The behaviour is defensible under §1.2's 'must stop once a non-null terminal state is reached' clause and is pinned by the R10 discriminants, but the operator-facing text no longer matches the code.

The GT-5 zsh test returns early with console.warn when zsh is not on PATH, so it reports as passing rather than skipped. On the target machine zsh always exists, but it.skip / expect-driven gating would make the absence visible instead of green.

Identity and evidence basis for this review: the supplied identities satisfy HEAD == input_commit == subject_commit == 745cfcad7018e026c48b172ab68ab8d57b4058ba and implementation_subject_commit 617f0ba815bb1cb5e062e6956ec043bf0f88b6be != subject_commit; the deterministic seal verifies actual Git HEAD. The spec was read at .dev-dispatch/spec/approved.md as named by spec_ref, and the committed .dev-dispatch/spec/manifest.json independently records the same spec_digest and path; content-hash recomputation is left to the seal, since this reviewer has read-only file inspection and executed no shell or Git command. The Continuous verdict committed in RC (rc-attempt_01KZTDQRF5K08RYC4ZJ6N8EDCP, APPROVE, zero findings, reviewer glm/code-plan) was read as feedback only — this Final judgment is independent and adds the findings above. Acceptance criteria 1–7 rest on the Implementer's acceptance-command results per §5; criteria 9–11 are the dispatcher's real-machine gate. Substantively verified by reading: GT-2 nested-escaped result parsing with named per-step loud failures, GT-7 line-wise JSON.parse with no brace regex anywhere on the summary path, GT-6 three-way classification (drained/exit 0 and max_rounds/exit 1 both continue; other non-zero exits and unparseable summaries fail immediately), GT-4 gate rewritten to real JSON parsing with 'stop on non-null terminal state', GT-5 zsh-safe splitting exercised by a real zsh run, GT-8 fake bus returning no head_seq on single-channel GET, profile-declared backoff/attempt/wall-clock limits, and per-round appends to drain-attempts.jsonl. The cross-drain tests genuinely spawn bin/e0-regression.sh with executable stubs rather than reimplementing the loop.
